one_line: A drop-in SDK that wraps an LLM client, saves raw turns to the user's own SQL database, sends each exchange to Memori's hosted 'Advanced Augmentation' service for facts, triples and a rolling conversation summary, and puts the top 5 facts (plus their conversation summaries) into the system prompt on the next call.

arch.product.t: Python SDK (plus TypeScript SDK, Rust core with PyO3/napi bindings, MCP server, Claude Code/OpenClaw/Hermes plugins). Two modes: BYODB (conn= given: raw turns, facts, graph in your database) and Cloud (no conn: everything goes to api.memorilabs.ai). In both modes, extraction runs on Memori's hosted service.

arch.truth.t: Raw messages in memori_conversation_message are kept; derived facts, triples and summaries sit beside them. Raw turns are only ever fed back as same-conversation history, never searched.

arch.stores.t: Relational only. Drivers for SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, TiDB, Oracle, OceanBase, CockroachDB (via PostgreSQL), and MongoDB, accessed through SQLAlchemy, DB-API, Django or pymongo adapters. Embeddings are stored as BLOBs in memori_entity_fact and scanned in process; there is no vector database.

arch.graphdb.t: No graph database. Triples are normalised into memori_subject / memori_predicate / memori_object / memori_knowledge_graph SQL tables with num_times. Recall never reads them; they exist for SQL querying and dashboards.

arch.scope.t: Attribution is entity_id (user, max 100 chars), process_id (agent) and session_id (UUID per instance). Facts and triples are scoped per entity and shared across processes. Process attributes are scoped per process. A conversation rolls over after 30 min of inactivity.
arch.scope.e: memori/__init__.py:188-215; _config.py:93; sqlite/_driver.py:37-66; docs advanced-augmentation.mdx extraction table (read/doc)

write.entry.t: Implicit: wrapping the client with mem.llm.register(client) monkey-patches create/stream methods for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, xAI, LangChain, Agno and Pydantic-AI. After the response, handle_post_response writes the turn and queues augmentation. The agent-style path is explicit: capture_agent_turn(user, assistant, trace).

write.receipt.t: Raw turn writes are synchronous: committed in the caller's thread after the LLM returns, before the caller gets control back. Augmentation is fire-and-forget on an asyncio runtime (max 50 workers in Python, 32 in Rust). Derived writes go through a 1,000-slot batch queue (batches of 100, 0.1 s). No receipt or job id is returned; mem.augmentation.wait() is the only barrier.

write.roles.t: System messages are dropped before storage. User and assistant text are both stored and both sent to extraction. Messages injected by Memori (history) are excluded via _memori_injected_count. Tool messages are stored but stripped on replay.

write.firewall.t: Not found. Retrieved facts go into the system prompt inside a <memori_context> tag with one hedge sentence. No sanitisation, trust score or injection screen. OpenClaw has a sanitizer.ts for its own plugin only.

write.governance.t: Entity and process ids are SHA-256 hashed before going to the augmentation API, but message content goes to Memori's servers in plain text. No redaction, consent or retention policy in code. The README mentions governance features in an open PR (#632).

segment.unit.t: One wrapped LLM call, i.e. one exchange. When a conversation summary already exists, only the latest user+assistant pair plus the stored summary goes to the extractor (Python path). The Rust path, default in BYODB, sends the call's messages with summary=None.

segment.rule.t: No topic segmentation. Conversation boundaries come from a 30-minute inactivity timeout per session_id or an explicit new_session().

segment.measured.t: Not found. The vendor benchmark processed each LoCoMo session into one set of triples plus one summary (so about 272 summaries), but call counts are not published.

extract.calls.t: One hosted call (POST sdk/augmentation or cloud/augmentation) per wrapped LLM call. The LLM, prompts and internal call count behind it are closed. Legacy v2 ran a local MemoryAgent (default gpt-4o) per exchange.

extract.facts.t: The service returns entity.facts and/or semantic triples (subject name+type, predicate, object name+type). When only triples come back, facts are synthesised as 'subject predicate object' strings. Docs list fact, preference, skill, rule and event types, but the stored rows carry no type column.

extract.episode.t: A rolling conversation-level summary is returned and stored in memori_conversation.summary, overwritten on each update. It serves as the episode layer and is attached to recalled facts through the fact-mention table.

extract.dates.t: Stored facts carry no event date. At read time, facts are labelled 'Stated at <date_created>' and summaries '[<date>]', both based on ingestion time. The payload has no field for the original conversation timestamp, so replayed history gets wrong dates. The vendor benchmark used precomputed memories that have LoCoMo session timestamps.
extract.dates.e: recall_injection.py:47-49,99-103; _models.py payload (read); OmniMemEval memori_client.py payload has no date (read); benchmarks 01 nb _summary/timestamp (read)

extract.neighbours.t: The extractor sees the current conversation summary (Python path) but not existing stored facts.

extract.failure.t: API failures are logged and the turn's derived memories are silently dropped (no retry queue). On 429, an anonymous user gets QuotaExceededError, which disables augmentation for the instance; a keyed user gets {}. Embedding failure writes facts without embeddings. The DB writer drops tasks when the queue is full after 5 s.

graph.entities.t: Subject and object entities with a lower-cased type come from the hosted NER/triple step.

graph.resolution.t: String-level only. Subjects and objects are deduplicated by sha256 of the lower-cased, alphanumeric-only name+type (generate_uniq). There is no alias or embedding resolution.

graph.edges.t: memori_knowledge_graph rows (entity, subject, predicate, object), unique per entity, with num_times and date_last_time on conflict.

time.fields.t: date_created, date_updated, date_last_time and num_times on facts and triples. No valid-from/to and no event time.

time.update.t: No contradiction or supersede logic. A changed fact is a new row; both stay recallable. Recency only affects which 1,000 embeddings are loaded.

time.dedup.t: Exact-text dedup: UNIQUE(entity_id, uniq), where uniq = sha256 of lower-cased alphanumerics. A repeat increments num_times and refreshes date_last_time. Same for triples and process attributes. No semantic dedup.

derive.session.t: Rolling per-conversation summary from the hosted service (see extract.episode). Cloud also exposes agent recall_summary and compaction endpoints.

derive.profile.t: No profile record in v3. The entity's fact set acts as the profile, and process attributes describe the agent. Legacy v2 had conscious_ingest: is_user_context/promotion_eligible memories were copied to short_term_memory and injected once at conversation start.

derive.background.t: Only per-turn async augmentation. No sleep-time consolidation in the SDK. Legacy v2 ran a conscious-agent loop every 5 minutes.

derive.forget.t: Docs claim 'intelligent ranking and decay', but no decay is in the code. Ranking is cosine+BM25 only. The only recency effect is the ORDER BY date_last_time DESC LIMIT 1000 candidate cap. Manual delete_entity_memories exists.

index.embed.t: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-d) run locally through Rust fastembed/ONNX; override with MEMORI_EMBEDDINGS_MODEL. The vendor benchmark used EmbeddingGemma-300M instead.

index.lexical.t: BM25 (k1 1.2, b 0.75, stopword list) computed in memory only over the dense candidate pool, not over the full store. There is no database FTS index in v3. Legacy v2 had SQLite FTS5.

index.vector.t: No ANN index. Up to recall_embeddings_limit=1000 most-recent embeddings per entity are loaded as BLOBs and scored by brute-force cosine (Rust, or the Python FAISS helper). Older facts beyond 1,000 cannot be recalled.

read.rewrite.t: None in v3. The query is the last user message text. Legacy v2 had an LLM retrieval agent (gpt-4o) that planned searches.

read.analysis.t: Only query length: queries of 2 or fewer content tokens raise the BM25 weight from 0.15 to 0.30.

read.legs.t: One dense leg; BM25 re-scores the dense top max(10*limit, 50) candidates. No separate lexical, graph or summary leg. Summaries only come along attached to their facts.

read.temporal.t: No time filter or temporal parsing. Dates are only printed next to facts and summaries.

read.traversal.t: The triple tables are never read at recall.

rank.fusion.t: SDK: linear blend rank = (1-w)*cosine + w*BM25(normalised to max), w=0.15 (0.30 for short queries), clamped to 0.05-0.40, env-tunable. The vendor benchmark used RRF (k=60) over separate FAISS and BM25 rankings instead, so the published numbers are not from the SDK ranker.

rank.gate.t: recall_relevance_threshold=0.1 on rank_score; if nothing passes, nothing is injected. The prompt hedge says to use context only if relevant.

rank.agentic.t: Not in the SDK auto path. Cloud agent_recall exposes date, project, session, signal and source filters for tool-calling agents (MCP/OpenClaw recall tools), but the agent itself drives it.

answer.shape.t: Appended to the system prompt: <memori_context>, a hedge line, 'Relevant context about the user:', top-5 facts as '- fact. Stated at date', then '## Summaries' with deduplicated conversation summaries linked to those facts. Separately, all messages of the current conversation from the DB are prepended as history (BYODB), or the cloud-returned messages (Cloud).

answer.size.t: Vendor: 1,294 tokens (paper) then 721 (docs), top-10 triples + summaries in the benchmark notebook. Independent OmniMemEval cloud run: 8,139 tokens (LoCoMo) and 2,779 (LME-S); the cloud recall also returns conversation messages. The SDK default is 5 facts + summaries + full current-conversation history, so the size grows with the conversation.
answer.size.e: arXiv 2603.19935 Table 2; results.mdx Table 2; OmniMemEval results.md:95,146; memori_client.py format sections 'Conversation Context, Facts, Summaries' (read)

answer.prompt.t: SDK: the injection block above, with no answer instructions. Benchmark: an answer prompt telling the model to use memories first, summaries for broader context, and to turn relative time into absolute dates using memory timestamps. The judge prompt is lenient on time formats.

eval.best.t: 87.0 (docs, 721 tokens) and 81.95 (paper, 1,294 tokens); both vendor-run, cat 1-4, gpt-4.1-mini reader and judge, 3-run mean.

eval.outside.t: OmniMemEval (MemTensor), Memori cloud: 41.34 overall (T 22.53), 8,139 tokens; LME-S 20.80 (SS-Asst 1.79, Know-Upd 6.41). This is a 40-46 point gap from the vendor figures. Inferred causes: (1) ingestion through the live API puts ingest time instead of LoCoMo session dates into 'Stated at', which collapses temporal; (2) the vendor numbers re-ranked downloaded precomputed memories with a different embedder (Gemma-300M) and RRF k=60, top-10, not the shipped SDK/cloud recall; (3) a different judge (gpt-4o-mini vs a lenient gpt-4.1-mini prompt).
eval.outside.e: OmniMemEval docs/user_memory/results.md:57,95,146; benchmarks/01 nb AA_MEMORIES_URL (precomputed json from lborro/memori-aa-data) (read); causes inferred

eval.models.t: Vendor: gpt-4.1-mini answers, gpt-4.1-mini judge, temperature 0. OmniMemEval: gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14 answers, gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 judge. The extraction model is undisclosed in both.
eval.models.e: benchmarks/02 nb OPENAI_MODEL, temperature=0; OmniMemEval results.md:25-27; arXiv paper (no extraction model named)

eval.rigour.t: Weak. Extraction is closed and was not rerun by the notebooks (memories are downloaded as JSON). Retrieval in the benchmark differs from the SDK. The paper counts 1,529 cat 1-4 questions vs the usual 1,540. Baseline numbers are copied from prior work, not rerun. Two vendor numbers (81.95, 87.0) exist with no changelog between them. The judge prompt is lenient on dates.

cost.write.t: About one hosted augmentation call per wrapped LLM call, so about 2,941 calls if LoCoMo is replayed as user/assistant pairs (5,882 turns); the vendor batched per session (272). Undisclosed internal LLM calls. Local cost is embedding only (MiniLM on CPU).

cost.read.t: Zero LLM calls on recall: one local query embedding + one SQL fetch of up to 1,000 BLOBs + one fetch of facts/summaries. Cloud mode is one HTTP call.

cost.where.t: Hybrid. Extraction is always on Memori's hosted service (free and rate-limited per IP when anonymous; an API key raises the limits). Embeddings and retrieval run locally in BYODB; everything runs hosted in Cloud mode.

trust.provenance.t: memori_entity_fact_mention links each fact to the conversation(s) it came from, used to attach summaries. No turn-level span, speaker or confidence. Triples have no source link.

trust.erasure.t: delete_entity_memories (BYODB only) deletes the entity's facts and knowledge-graph rows but keeps conversations, messages and summaries. There is no deletion on the hosted extraction side.

trust.auth.t: BYODB inherits database credentials. Cloud uses MEMORI_API_KEY (Bearer/X-Memori-API-Key). Anonymous augmentation is allowed with an IP quota. No per-entity ACL.

trust.sharing.t: Facts are per entity and shared by every process (agent) using that entity_id; process attributes are per agent. No grants or read/write policies.

extras.t: Monkey-patches the provider SDK methods (sync, async, stream) so capture and recall need no extra code; history and facts are injected per provider format.
When a conversation summary exists, the extractor gets only the summary + latest user/assistant pair, not the whole conversation. This keeps extraction cost flat per turn.
Facts are the index and conversation summaries the payload: each recalled fact pulls its source conversation summary via the mention table, deduplicated, so only a few summaries enter context.
A separate per-agent memory (memori_process_attribute) of what the agent handles; agent trace capture (tool calls, outcomes) via capture_agent_turn/OpenClaw.
Memori.provision(provider='tidb-zero') creates a database. An MCP server and Claude Code/OpenClaw/Hermes plugins expose recall, recall_summary, compaction, feedback and quota tools.

v2.x: conscious_ingest copied memories flagged essential/is_user_context/promotion_eligible into short_term_memory and injected them once per conversation (working memory). auto_ingest searched long_term_memory (limit 5) on every call via an LLM retrieval agent. A background conscious agent ran every 5 min. Removed in v3.

token_economy.t: Per-turn context: up to recall_facts_limit=5 facts (relevance threshold 0.1), each a short triple-like sentence with a date, plus the deduplicated conversation summaries those facts came from, appended to the system prompt. Compression happens at write time (closed hosted extractor turns exchanges into triples and a rolling summary); there is no read-time budget, truncation or compression. Vendor-measured added context: 1,294 tokens (paper), then 721 (docs). Two things work against this: (a) BYODB prepends every message of the current conversation as history (session-bounded only by the 30-min timeout), and (b) the independent cloud run measured 8,139 tokens, which suggests the cloud recall also returns conversation messages. Write side: the extractor sees summary + last exchange only, and exact-hash dedup collapses repeated facts.
token_economy.e: _config.py:87-88; recall_injection.py:170-224; conversation_injection.py:215-225; _augmentation.py:53-84; arXiv 2603.19935 Table 2; results.mdx Table 2; OmniMemEval results.md:95 (read/doc)

speed.t: Write: the raw turn is committed synchronously after the LLM response. Augmentation is async (asyncio runtime with a semaphore of 50 in Python, or a Rust tokio worker with queue 256 and concurrency 32, the BYODB default). Derived writes are batched by a single writer thread (100 per batch, 0.1 s window, 1,000-slot queue, drop on full). Augmentation HTTP timeout is 5 s in Python and 30 s in Rust. Read: no LLM; one local MiniLM embedding (Rust fastembed), brute-force cosine over at most 1,000 BLOBs, BM25 over at most 50 candidates, partial sort in Rust. No published latency numbers found.

keep: Facts as the index, summaries as the payload: retrieve small facts, then attach their source episode summary via a mention table (cheap multi-layer context).
Write-time incremental extraction from rolling summary + last exchange keeps extractor tokens flat per turn.
Zero-LLM read path with a relevance gate (inject nothing below threshold) and a query-length-adaptive dense/BM25 weight.
Exact-hash dedup with num_times / date_last_time counters is a cheap first-pass reinforcement signal.
Raw turn persistence is synchronous and separate from async derivation, so raw truth survives extraction failure.
avoid: Ingest-time dates as 'Stated at' with no event-time field: replayed or imported history loses its timeline (likely cause of T 22.53 in the independent run).
A brute-force scan of the 1,000 most recent embeddings per entity makes older facts unreachable, and BM25 only re-scores dense candidates, so lexical misses can't be recovered.
Closed hosted extractor with silent drop on failure/quota: no retry, no local fallback, content leaves the user's database despite 'BYODB'.
Benchmark/SDK mismatch (precomputed memories, a different embedder, RRF top-10) gives vendor 81.95-87.0 vs independent 41.34; docs claim 'decay' that is not in the code.
